title: ～たがる — a third person “wants to ～”
summary: The third-person version of ～たい. Add たがる to the verb stem to describe someone other than yourself wanting to do something. It is usually used as ～たがっている.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形の語幹＋たがる
patterns.gloss: Verb stem + たがる (行きたがる)

body.p: ～たい states the speaker’s own wish (or asks the listener’s). When you observe another person’s wish from outside, such as a younger brother or a child, use ～たがる.
For a wish present right now, use ～たがっている. For a habit or tendency, ～たがる works (子どもは甘いものばかり食べたがる).

examples.ja: 弟（おとうと）は外（そと）へ行（い）きたがっています。
examples.romaji: Otōto wa soto e ikitagatte imasu.
examples.tr: My little brother wants to go outside.

examples.ja: 妹（いもうと）は新（あたら）しい服（ふく）を買（か）いたがっている。
examples.romaji: Imōto wa atarashii fuku o kaitagatte iru.
examples.tr: My little sister wants to buy new clothes.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもは甘（あま）いものばかり食（た）べたがる。
examples.romaji: Kodomo wa amai mono bakari tabetagaru.
examples.tr: The child always wants to eat only sweet things.

pitfalls: Not for your own wishes (× 私は行きたがる).
The thing wanted takes を (ケーキを食べたがる).
